outages.cause: Rolling and emergency blackouts after Russian attacks on energy infrastructure
outages.affected: Ukrenergo said hourly rolling blackouts of 1.5 to 3 queues for all consumers, plus industrial capacity limits, are in effect around the clock in parts of Ukraine on Saturday, Nov 14. New Saturday-morning outages: DTEK said a Russian attack on one of its facilities in the north of Odesa region left almost 50,000 households without power (no restoration time given); Sumyoblenergo reported a large-scale emergency outage in part of Sumy region (no customer count released for security reasons); DTEK said emergency cuts are in effect in the Bucha, Fastiv, and Obukhiv districts of Kyiv region, with stabilization schedules in Kyiv city and the rest of the region. Poltava regional authorities said bad weather left about 2,000 subscribers in 13 settlements without power. On Friday, Nov 13, Chernihivoblenergo said an attack left about 150,000 customers without power in the Nizhyn and Pryluky districts, and the Energy Ministry said consumers in 12 regions were without power; no later Chernihiv figure was found.
outages.updated: Nov 14, 2026, morning Kyiv time (UNN 8:59 a.m.; DTEK Odesa figure per Ukrainska Pravda 12:32 p.m. EET = 4:32 a.m. CT); rechecked 5:53 AM CT

outages.cause: Russian attack on a DTEK energy facility
outages.affected: Almost 50,000 households without power, according to DTEK. Crews were clearing rubble and repairing damaged equipment; DTEK said the facility had been hit repeatedly and restoration will take time.

outages.cause: Generation capacity deficit, with the Antonio Guiteras, Ernesto Guevara (Santa Cruz), and Felton plants all fully offline due to breakdowns and maintenance
outages.affected: UNE's latest daily bulletin (Friday, Nov 13) forecast 1,930 MW affected at peak: 900 MW available versus 2,800 MW demand (1,900 MW deficit), after a Thursday maximum of 1,920 MW at 7:00 p.m. and service affected all 24 hours. On Friday, Granma and Las Tunas were each briefly cut off from the national grid and reconnected with only 20 MW and 15 MW, respectively. As of 4:02 a.m. Saturday Cuba time, the Electric Company of Havana reported 258 MW affected and 117 distribution circuits out in Havana, with some circuits in Boyeros out for nearly 14 hours. CiberCuba's SEN observatory (updated 5:01 a.m. Saturday) still lists the national grid as interconnected, with no total collapse recorded. UNE's Saturday bulletin had not been published as of early Saturday CT.
outages.updated: Nov 14, 2026, 5:45 a.m. Cuba time (4:45 a.m. CT), per CiberCuba's latest Havana circuit notices; rechecked 5:53 AM CT

outages.cause: Widespread, ongoing grid failures after years of underinvestment and poor maintenance, worsened by June earthquakes
outages.affected: No official customer count. Bloomberg Línea reported Nov 13 that outages are worsening nationwide, with Mérida, Táchira, and Trujillo among the hardest hit; Caracas is largely spared the worst cuts. France 24 reported Nov 13 that some communities in Carabobo state go up to eight hours a day without power. A late-September Meganálisis survey cited by Bloomberg Línea found 87% of respondents lost power at least four days a week. Interim President Delcy Rodríguez said the June earthquakes took about 800 MW of generation offline, of which 600 MW had been restored.
outages.updated: Nov 13, 2026 (Bloomberg Línea and France 24); rechecked 5:53 AM CT, no official customer count found

outages.cause: National generation shortfall during evening peak; Tarbela hydropower about 800 MW below normal after reduced water releases following the fifth-extension incident, plus seasonal hydrology and LNG limits
outages.affected: About 1,500 MW national shortfall during evening peak on Nov 11 (peak demand about 16,000 MW vs. about 14,500 MW available), according to ISMO figures cited Nov 12. ISMO said the Nov 10 shortfall, which reached about 2,530 MW, had eased and that generation was back to the routine plan as of Nov 11, but the 1,500 MW evening-peak gap (5 p.m. to 11 p.m.) remained. Discos were following existing 1.5 to 2 hour load-management schedules; The Nation reported some areas still facing up to five hours of additional load-shedding. No later official ISMO update was found as of early Saturday CT.
outages.updated: Nov 12, 2026; no later official ISMO update found as of 5:53 AM CT

outages.place: Mayfair, Crosby, Homestead Park, Mayfair West, and nearby suburbs
outages.cause: Fire and a later explosion at the Mayfair substation; after a Thursday-night restoration, the Hursthill substation tripped early Friday because of a network overload. The cause of the Mayfair fire is being investigated
outages.affected: No official customer count. In a Saturday, Nov 14, customer alert, City Power said it had restored electricity to the SABC, Netcare Garden City Hospital, and residential customers in Mayfair West after overnight repairs and testing at the Hursthill and Mayfair substations. A Friday morning attempt to restore more customers was interrupted when the network became overloaded and supply tripped again. City Power said Saturday that engineers would continue preparing for Phase 2, which is expected to restore remaining affected customers if there are no further technical challenges. A separate Hursthill SDC update issued at 7:30 a.m. SAST Saturday said that centre was managing 1,524 open calls, 1,266 of them more than 24 hours old; that figure covers the wider Hursthill service area and is not a customer count for the Mayfair outage alone.
outages.etr: City Power said Saturday that Phase 2 is expected to restore remaining customers if there are no further technical challenges
